Cite this lesson Video Summary for False Imprisonment False imprisonment is a crime where a person is held against their will through physical restraint, threats, or coercion. This differs from kidnapping, which involves both abduction and false imprisonment. For false imprisonment to exist, there must be no legal justification, the person must be held against their will, the victim must believe they are confined, and the captor must intentionally be keeping them from leaving. Cases like McCann v. Wal-Mart and the Groppetti incident demonstrate different aspects of false imprisonment. Perpetrators may face both criminal charges (misdemeanors or felonies) and civil lawsuits. False imprisonment does not apply to legally justified detention The victim must be held against their will The victim must believe they are confined The captor must intentionally prevent the victim from leaving This video explains how false imprisonment differs from other detention situations.
